24236-time-and-tide-a-romance-of-the-moo.title: on the Afternoons of November 19 and 26, 1888.
24236-time-and-tide-a-romance-of-the-moo.creator: Sir Robert S. Ball, Ll.D., F.R.S.,
24236-time-and-tide-a-romance-of-the-moo.description: A book by Sir Robert S. Ball, Ll.D., F.R.S.,. dress you this afternoon on a subject in which science and poetry are blended in a happy conjunction. If there be a peculiar fascination about the earlier chapters of any branch of history, how great must be the interest which attaches to that most primeval of all terrestrial histories which relates to the actual beginnings of this globe on which we stand.

arxiv-2204-13323.title: Discriminative-Region Attention and Orthogonal-View Generation Model for Vehicle Re-Identification
arxiv-2204-13323.creator: First Huadong Li, Second Yuefeng Wang, Third Ying Wei, Fourth Lin Wang, Fifth Li Ge
arxiv-2204-13323.description: Abstract Vehicle re-identiﬁcation (Re-ID) is urgently demanded to alleviate the pressure caused by the increasingly onerous task of urban traffic management. Multiple challenges hamper the applications of vision-based vehicle Re-ID methods: (1) The appearances of different vehicles of the same brand/model are often similar; However, (2) the appearances of the same vehicle differ significantly from different viewpoints.

arxiv-2205-11650.title: Spin Tetrad Formalism Of Circular Polarization States In Relativistic Jets
arxiv-2205-11650.creator: Ronald S. Gamble, Jr
arxiv-2205-11650.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ronald S. Gamble, Jr. Relativistic jets from active galactic nuclei (AGN) have been of peak interest in the high-energy astrophysics community for their uniquely dynamic nature and incredible radiative power; emanating from supermassive black holes and similarly accreting compact dense objects. An overall consensus on relativistic jet formation states that accelerated outflow at high Lorentz factors are generated by a complex relationship between the accretion disk of the system and the frame-dragging effects of the rotating massive central object.

arxiv-2311-09389.title: Neural machine translation for automated feedback on children’s early-stage writing
arxiv-2311-09389.creator: Jonas Vestergaard Jensen, Mikkel Jordahn, Michael Riis Andersen
arxiv-2311-09389.description: Abstract In this work, we address the problem of assessing and constructing feedback for early-stage writing automatically using machine learning. Early-stage writing is typically vastly different from conventional writing due to phonetic spelling and lack of proper grammar, punctuation, spacing etc. Consequently, early-stage writing is highly non-trivial to analyze using common linguistic metrics.

arxiv-2405-10761.title: Critical feature learning in deep neural networks
arxiv-2405-10761.creator: Kirsten Fischer, Javed Lindner, David Dahmen, Zohar Ringel, Michael Krämer, Moritz Helias
arxiv-2405-10761.description: Abstract A key property of neural networks driving their success is their ability to learn features from data. Understanding feature learning from a theoretical viewpoint is an emerging field with many open questions. In this work we capture finite-width effects with a systematic theory of network kernels in deep non-linear neural networks.

arxiv-2409-13540.title: FullAnno: A Data Engine for Enhancing Image Comprehension of MLLMs
arxiv-2409-13540.creator: Jing Hao, Yuxiang Zhao, Song Chen, Yanpeng Sun, Qiang Chen, Gang Zhang, Kun Yao, Errui Ding, Jingdong Wang
arxiv-2409-13540.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jing Hao, Yuxiang Zhao, Song Chen, Yanpeng Sun, Qiang Chen, Gang Zhang, Kun Yao, Errui Ding, Jingdong Wang. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have shown promise in a broad range of vision-language tasks with their strong reasoning and generalization capabilities. However, they heavily depend on high-quality data in the Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) phase.

arxiv-2410-10125.title: Generative Deep Learning and Signal Processing for Data Augmentation of Cardiac Auscultation Signals: Improving Model Robustness Using Synthetic Audio
arxiv-2410-10125.creator: Leigh Abbott, Milan Marocchi, Matthew Fynn, Yue Rong, Sven Nordholm
arxiv-2410-10125.description: Abstract Accurately interpreting cardiac auscultation signals is essential for diagnosing and managing cardiovascular diseases. However, the paucity of labelled data inhibits classification models’ training. Researchers have turned to generative deep learning techniques alongside signal processing to augment existing data and improve cardiac auscultation classification models. However, the primary focus of prior studies has been on model performance rather than robustness.

arxiv-2501-11815.title: CogMorph : Cognitive Morphing Attacks for Text-to-Image Models
arxiv-2501-11815.creator: Zonglei Jing, Zonghao Ying, Le Wang, Siyuan Liang, Aishan Liu, Xianglong Liu, Dacheng Tao
arxiv-2501-11815.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Zonglei Jing, Zonghao Ying, Le Wang, Siyuan Liang, Aishan Liu, Xianglong Liu, Dacheng Tao. The development of text-to-image (T2I) generative models, that enable the creation of high-quality synthetic images from textual prompts, has opened new frontiers in creative design and content generation.

arxiv-2502-11438.title: SAFE-SQL: Self-Augmented In-Context Learning with Fine-grained Example Selection for Text-to-SQL
arxiv-2502-11438.creator: Jimin Lee, Ingeol Baek, Byeongjeong Kim, Hyunkyung Bae, Hwanhee Lee
arxiv-2502-11438.description: Abstract Text-to-SQL aims to convert natural language questions into executable SQL queries. While previous approaches, such as skeleton-masked selection, have demonstrated strong performance by retrieving similar training examples to guide large language models (LLMs), they struggle in real-world scenarios where such examples are unavailable.

arxiv-2503-07999.title: Complete Measurement of Two-Photon Density Matrix by Single-Photon Detection
arxiv-2503-07999.creator: Salini Rajeev, Mayukh Lahiri
arxiv-2503-07999.description: Abstract The reconstruction of density matrices from measurement data (quantum state tomography) is the most comprehensive method for assessing the accuracy and performance of quantum devices. Existing methods to reconstruct two-photon density matrices require the detection of both photons unless a priori information is available.

arxiv-2605-14709.title: Breaking Dual Bottlenecks: Evolving Unified Multimodal Models into Self-Adaptive Interleaved Visual Reasoners
arxiv-2605-14709.creator: Qingyang Liu, Bingjie Gao, Canmiao Fu, Zhipeng Huang, Chen Li, Feng Wang, Shuochen Chang, Shaobo Wang, Yali Wang, Keming Ye, Jiangtong Li, Li Niu

europmc-pmc6700281.creator: Genetic Modifiers of Huntington’s Disease (GeM-HD) Consortium. Electronic address: gusella@helix.mgh.harvard.edu, Genetic Modifiers of Huntington’s Disease (GeM-HD) Consortium.
europmc-pmc6700281.description: Variable, glutamine-encoding, CAA interruptions indicate that a property of the uninterrupted HTT CAG repeat sequence, distinct from the length of huntingtin's polyglutamine segment, dictates the rate at which Huntington's disease (HD) develops. The timing of onset shows no...

lotze-logic-bosanquet-1884.title: Logic, in Three Books: Of Thought, of Investigation, and of Knowledge
lotze-logic-bosanquet-1884.creator: Hermann Lotze (Bernard Bosanquet, trans. and ed.)
lotze-logic-bosanquet-1884.description: Lotze’s System of Philosophy, Part I: his complete logic — of thought, of investigation, of knowledge — in Bosanquet’s 1884 Clarendon Press translation; the English form in which Lotze shaped British idealism and early analytic philosophy.

pmc-10607999.title: Five New Species of Aureoboletus and Chalciporus (Boletaceae, Boletales) and Their Ethnomycological Aspects
pmc-10607999.creator: Olivia Ayala-Vásquez, Magdalena Martínez-Reyes, Jesús Pérez-Moreno, César Ramiro Martínez-González, Juan Pablo Pinzón, Javier Isaac de la Fuente, Rigoberto Castro-Rivera, Jesús García-Jiménez, Soledad Balbuena-Carrasco, Eliseete Ramírez-Carbajal, Fuqiang Yu
pmc-10607999.description: Among Boletales, the family Boletaceae has the highest diversity worldwide. Additionally, this fungal group has great ecological relevance because it not only includes mainly ectomycorrhizal but also saprotrophic species. Furthermore, some species are used as food and have sociocultural and economic importance worldwide.

pmc-10618524.title: The metagenomic and metabolomic profile of the gut microbes in Chinese full-term and late preterm infants treated with Clostridium butyricum
pmc-10618524.creator: Hong Li, Xingling Ma, Yongfu Li, Qin Liu, Qiuyan Tian, Xiaofeng Yang, Zhemin Zhou, Jing Ren, Bin Sun, Xing Feng, Hong Zhang, Xiaoping Yin, Heng Li, Xin Ding
pmc-10618524.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The present study investigated the composition, abundance, and diversity of gut microbes in full-term and late-preterm infants from a medical center in eastern China. A total of 144 genomes of stool samples were captured for 16S rRNA metagenomic analyses. A high abundance of commensal intestinal bacteria was detected in these samples such as Phocaeicola vulgatus, Escherichia coli, and Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, indicating a relatively consistent diversity of gut microbes in the present full-term infants aged 38–40 weeks.

pmc-11415748.title: Agentivité : perspectives des ergothérapeutes quant à leur sentiment de compétence et quant à leurs compétences à la suite d’une formation
pmc-11415748.creator: Annie Carrier, Alexandra Éthier, Michaël Beaudoin, Anne Hudon, Denis Bédard, Emmanuelle Jasmin, Étienne Lavoie-Trudeau, France Verville
pmc-11415748.description: ContextePour s’attaquer aux injustices systémiques vécues par les personnes en situation de vulnérabilité, l’agentivité des ergothérapeutes, soit leur pouvoir d’agir, est nécessaire. Or, elles se sentent peu compétentes à l’exercer et aimeraient développer leurs compétences. L’objectif général de cette recherche était donc de documenter la perception des ergothérapeutes de leurs compétences avant et à la suite d’une formation à l’agentivité.

pmc-11518058.title: Family: cornerstone for young people to be victims of violence in the university stage
pmc-11518058.creator: J Villegas-Dominguez, A Estrada Cancino, R A Hernandez Hernandez, A E Caldare Ojeda, J C Viñaz Dozal, F Ruiz Garcia, Y R Sosa Gonzalez
pmc-11518058.description: IntroductionViolence is a pervasive issue that wreaks havoc within communities, with the family serving as a cornerstone for the development of individuals, thereby influencing their behavior within society.ObjectivesTo determine the association between a history of family violence and being a victim of violence among university students.MethodologyThis is a cross-sectional, prospective study that included university students of both sexes.

pmc-11532098.title: Editorial: Effects of nonpharmacological interventions on HbA1c variability and glycemic control
pmc-11532098.creator: João Soares Felício
pmc-11532098.description: l for achieving diabetes treatment goals and maximizing quality of life (1). Essential to achieving these goals are diabetes self-management education and support (DSMES), nutrition therapy, routine physical activity, health behavior counseling, and psychosocial care (2). Among the main types approaches for diabetes mellitus (DM), the lifestyle change based on nutritional interventions and physical exercise stands out.

pmc-12397902.title: Genetic mapping of Ascochyta blight resistance in an ILL6002 × Indianhead lentil mapping population
pmc-12397902.creator: Em L Thackwray, Bernadette M Henares, Christina R Grime, Bethany L Clark, Robert C Lee, Lars G Kamphuis
pmc-12397902.description: Ascochyta blight of lentil (Lens culinaris Medik.) is a fungal disease caused by Ascochyta lentis. This study was carried out to identify the location of quantitative trait loci (QTL) associated with resistance from the accession Indianhead, and how these vary between the recently identified pathotypes of A. lentis.

pmc-12751337.title: Health and wellbeing experiences of women informal workers during the COVID-19 pandemic: a qualitative systematic review
pmc-12751337.creator: Siti Aishah Ibrahim, Iman Ghosh, Suat Yan Lai, Bronwyn Harris, Abimbola Ayorinde
pmc-12751337.description: BackgroundLacking social safety nets, women informal workers were adversely affected during the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly with their over-representation in hard-hit sectors and poor prospect of alternative employment. Differential needs of women informal workers during the pandemic must be explored to address health inequalities and inform pandemic preparedness.

pmc-12790033.title: High-Sensitivity Troponin I
pmc-12790033.creator: Pavel Martinez-Dominguez, Nilda Espinola-Zavaleta
pmc-12790033.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Corresponding Author In the evolving field of cardio-oncology, anthracycline-based regimens have transformed the prognosis of breast cancer and lymphoid malignancies, improving long-term survival and rendering many aggressive lymphomas largely curable.1 However, this carries the well-recognized liability of dose-dependent cardiotoxicity, ranging from asymptomatic heart failure and subclinical declines in global longitudinal strain (GLS) to a notorious decrease in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF).2 Survivors ultimately face increased cardiovascular mortality driven by cancer therapy–related cardiac dysfunction, which may manifest years after chemotherapy completion.3 High-sensitivity

pmc-13384437.title: Genome-wide association study of the reproductive, body size, and carcass-related latent and directly measured traits in admixed beef heifers
pmc-13384437.creator: Muhammad Anas, Bin Zhao, Haipeng Yu, Carl R. Dahlen, Kendall C. Swanson, Kris A. Ringwall, Lauren L. Hulsman Hanna
pmc-13384437.description: Latent variables derived through factor analysis reveal the underlying biological traits (UBT) in organisms. However, research on UBT development and genomic applications in beef cattle is limited. This study aimed to model previously identified economically important UBT in genome-wide association studies (GWAS) using univariate and multivariate approaches.

pmc-13385669.title: Genome-wide identification of the SnRK2 gene family and its response to drought stress in Bombax ceiba
pmc-13385669.creator: Yumei Shi, Zhifang Zhang, Ruoxin He, Liangju He, Yongxiu Wang, Wenjie Ma, Zhenghao Yan, Youqiang Tao, Zhi Yang, Changxin Luo
pmc-13385669.description: IntroductionDrought is a major abiotic stress limiting the growth and ecological adaptation of tropical and subtropical trees. The SnRK2 gene family is a core regulator in ABA signaling and drought response pathways. However, genome-wide identification and functional characterization of the SnRK2 family remain unclear in Bombax ceiba, a typical drought-tolerant tropical pioneer tree species with important ecological and economic value.

pmc-13423606.title: The intergenerational sequelae of dysfunctional conflict in the family of origin: Evidence from two samples
pmc-13423606.creator: Natasha A. Bailey, Austin J. Blake, Alexander K. Johansson, Jessica A. Stern, Meghan A. Costello, Laurie Chassin, Joseph P. Allen
pmc-13423606.description: This investigation examined pathways connecting dysfunctional conflict (parent and family aggression, parental psychological control) in adolescents’ families of origin to parenting of the next generation across two studies. Study 1 included 184 Generation 2 (G2) adolescents (58% White, 29% Black, 13% other identities; 99 females, 85 males) who provided data on their Generation 1 (G1) parents.

pmc-13524507.title: Microneedle delivery of 3D bioprinted tendon stem/progenitor cells microfiber-derived extracellular vesicles enhances chronic massive rotator cuff tears healing
pmc-13524507.creator: Weiping He, Xiaopeng Yin, Shihai Jiang, Yi Zhang, Boxun Liu, Zhifeng Zhang, Woquan Ye, Shurong He, Tao Xu, Chang Liu, Kun Wang
pmc-13524507.description: High retear rates after surgical repair of chronic massive rotator cuff tears (CMRCT) are primarily due to the failure to regenerate native tendon tissue. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from rat tendon stem/progenitor cells (rTSPCs) present substantial potential benefits for the treatment of CMRCT.

pmc-13581793.title: Testicular intestinal-type adenocarcinoma without an identifiable extratesticular primary site: a case report and literature review
pmc-13581793.creator: Jinrong Tang, Heng Jiang, Xiaoke Zeng
pmc-13581793.description: BackgroundTesticular intestinal-type adenocarcinoma is an exceedingly rare malignant neoplasm characterized by intestinal epithelial differentiation and accounts for only a minute proportion of testicular malignancies. Its imaging features remain insufficiently characterized and may overlap with those of other testicular tumors, particularly seminoma.
